crime_highlights: They assaulted one of the parties to that dispute by taking turns hitting him with a bat.
The victim had no weapon, was too intoxicated to defend himself and, at times, was on the ground.
The assault caused a long and deep laceration to the victim's scalp.
In the judge's view, the assault could have been fatal.
rationale_highlights: That is because the Crown's position and the judge's sentence both took significant account of Mr. Tom's experiences as an Indigenous person in Canada.
were mitigating and justified a sentence towards the bottom rather than towards the top of the usual range for an unprovoked aggravated assault with a weapon
His offending was driven, in large part, by his experiences as an Indigenous person in Canada.
The judge weighed the many aggravating features of his offence against the many mitigating features of his personal circumstances.
As a result of her balancing exercise, she imposed a sentence at the low end of the usual range.
note: Appeal court agrees Gladue factors mitigating, justified low-end sentence

crime_highlights: Mr. Murtagh was pushing her mother around inside their home
Mr. Murtagh had arrived approximately a week and a half prior, had thrown the complainant around every day since arriving
The neighbour's security system recorded Mr. Murtagh dragging the complainant away while she was screaming.
Mr. Murtagh had assaulted her and choked her so hard she could not breathe
The police observed bruising on the complainant's face and jaw consistent with her description of what occurred.
rationale_highlights: Mr. Murtagh is a member of the Siksika First Nation.
His life has been marred by many of the all-too-common direct and indirect adverse effects of Canada's colonial and post-colonial assimilationist policies.
note: Joint-submission appeal; appeal court never weighs Gladue factors itself

crime_highlights: The appellant chained herself to a gate in contravention of the injunction and obstructed a public roadway.
This time, she interfered with machinery belonging to one of the logging contractors
rationale_highlights: These included the intergenerational impact of family members having attended residential and Indian Day schools, children being removed from their homes
I appreciate that Gladue factors are also relevant to the choice of sanction
a cumulative 51-day sentence of imprisonment respects the principles of parity and totality, and takes account of the appellant's Gladue factors and efforts made at rehabilitation

But for the latter two aspects of this case, it is my view a fit cumulative sentence for seven offences of criminal contempt of the nature committed by Ms. Davidson, involving repeated and deliberate violations of more than one court order, would have required a substantially longer period of conventional imprisonment.
note: No reduced culpability, but Gladue factors shortened sentence (para 102)
